extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting short speculative (science fiction, fantasy, horror) fiction to Clarkesworld Magazine
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting short science fiction, fantasy, and horror stories to Clarkesworld Magazine, including length, format, rights, stylistic expectations, and submission/process rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and word length
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarkesworld Magazine pays 10¢ a word for works of science fiction, fantasy, and horror. We have a firm word limit of 4000 words. We will not consider stories longer than 4000 words or shorter than 1000 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not query about word lengths. Do not send stories shorter than 1000 or longer than 4000 words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights claimed
rubrics_metrics.description: We claim first world electronic rights, first print rights for the production of signed/numbered limited edition chapbooks (author must be willing to sign 100+ chapbooks), and non-exclusive anthology rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware of and accept these rights terms before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall writing quality / language
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be well-written. Language is important. There is no distinction between 'style' and 'substance' or 'story' and 'writing' — stories are made out of words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your story isn't worth reading as a collection of words, sentences, and paragraphs, it isn't worth experiencing in story form. Emphasize craft and language; poor prose will harm otherwise interesting ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-screen readability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very long paragraphs or typographical trickery may work against you. Format and paragraph length should suit reading on screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre-specific expectations (SF/Fantasy/Horror)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science fiction need not be 'hard' SF, but rigor is appreciated. Fantasy can be folkloric, medieval, contemporary, surreal, etc. Horror can be supernatural or psychological, so long as it is frightening.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigor/consistency is valued in SF; fantasy styles are wide-open; horror must effectively frighten. Submissions across these subgenres are acceptable within those expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of profanity, gore, and sexuality
rubrics_metrics.description: There are no barriers as to levels of profanity, gore, or sexuality allowed, but high amounts of profanity, gore, and sexuality are generally used poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you include heavy profanity, gore, or sexual content, be sure to use them well and with purpose; gratuitous excess is frowned upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard sells / content to avoid
rubrics_metrics.description: The following are likely hard sells: (list of unwanted tropes and story types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original text examples included: 'stories in which a milquetoast civilian government is depicted as the sole obstacle to either catching some depraved criminal or to an uncomplicated military victory'; 'stories in which the words "thou" or "thine" appear'; 'talking cats'; 'talking swords'; 'stories where the climax is dependent on the spilling of intestines'; 'stories where FTL travel is as easy as it is on television shows or movies'; 'time travel too'; 'stories that depend on some vestigial belief in Judeo-Christian mythology in order to be frightening'; 'stories about rapist-murderer-cannibals'; 'stories about young kids playing in some field and discovering ANYTHING'; 'stories about the stuff we all read in Scientific American three months ago'; 'stories where the Republicans, or Democrats, or Libertarians, or the Spartacist League, etc. take over the world and either save or ruin it'; 'your AD&D game'; '"funny" stories that depend on, or even include, puns'; 'sexy vampires, wanton werewolves, or lusty pirates'; 'stories where the protagonist is either widely despised or widely admired simply because he or she is just so smart and/or strange'; 'stories that take place within an artsy-fartsy bohemia as written by an author who has clearly never experienced one'; 'your trunk stories.' Use this list as concrete anti-pattern guidance when deciding whether to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and file format
rubrics_metrics.description: Email subs only to Nick Mamatas (clarkesfiction@gmail.com), either RTF or with text appended to the body of the email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not send paper submissions or other delivery methods. If emailing, include the story as RTF or paste the text into the message body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter content and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a cover letter — text appended to the body of the email — with publishing history and any other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor treats cover letters as a first impression: 'Some editors dutifully ignore cover letters until after reading the submission so as not to be influenced by their contents. Those editors do not work for Clarkesworld Magazine. A cover letter is what you wear and how you groom yourself for a job interview.' Mention relevant facts (e.g., if you wrote a lusty pirate story and happen to BE a lusty pirate, mention that).

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time and query policy
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive an emailed response to your submission within 50 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Please do not send queries until after this 50-day period has passed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No revisions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send revisions to a submission at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once submitted, the story is considered final for that submission; do not follow up with revised drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission and simultaneous-submission timing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers may not submit another story for a period of seven days after receiving a rejection. Please do not re-submit stories that have been rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect these timing rules; re-submitting rejected work or sending multiple stories too quickly may be treated negatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-acceptance submission blackout
rubrics_metrics.description: Writers whose work is accepted may not submit again until six months after their story is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If accepted, wait six months after publication before submitting new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not argue with rejection slips / don't game the guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not argue with rejection slips. If you are uncertain about anything above, we recommend following the most conservative interpretation. Please do not attempt to 'game' these submission guidelines, as it will just lead to them being rewritten to close loopholes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors prefer straightforward compliance and professional behavior. Attempting to exploit loopholes will backfire and may result in policy changes.
